# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I hold the manual, but I cannot speak, and I cannot touch the bomb. I can only communicate via gestures, and only Deaf can receive my gestures. Blind cannot see gestures at all, and Blind cannot hear me anyway since I can't speak.

This means I can never communicate directly with Blind. My only channel is to Deaf, who can see the bomb but cannot hear or receive gestures from anyone in a way that helps them relay to Blind... wait, actually Deaf can speak. So Deaf can gesture to me? No - Deaf can see, so Deaf receives gestures. Deaf speaks, which Blind can hear (Blind cannot hear - wait, Blind "cannot hear" per the table... let me recheck).

Actually the table says Blind "Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." It doesn't say Blind can't hear. Only Deaf cannot hear. So Blind CAN hear speech. Deaf can speak, and Blind can hear - so Deaf can relay information to Blind via speech, once Deaf learns it from me via gesture.

So the chain is: I (Mute) gesture to Deaf → Deaf learns the manual mapping → Deaf sees the bomb's light color → Deaf speaks the correct wire color to Blind (in the next round, since turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf).

I need to encode the manual using gestures. I'll assign gesture symbols to represent light colors and wire colors. Let me use simple distinct symbols per color, sent to Deaf only.

I'll signal the mapping using pairs of gestures: one for light color, one for cut color, using an agreed simple code. Since Deaf doesn't know my code yet, I need to establish it in this first message using distinguishable symbols per row.

Let me use: 👍=blue, ✌=green, 🖐=yellow (lights and wires same color words, reuse same symbol per color name).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "✌", "🖐", "🖐", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows 0. Light is blue. Three wires: 1 is green, 2 is yellow, 3 is red.

Deaf saw the bomb: light is blue, and wire 3 is red. According to my manual, blue → cut red. Wire 3 is red, so Blind should cut wire 3.

I need to get this to Deaf so Deaf can relay it to Blind via speech (since Deaf speaks and Blind can hear). I already sent a gesture code last turn: 👍=blue, ☝=(separator?), ✌=green, 🖐=yellow, 🖐=yellow, ✌=green — that was meant to convey blue→red, green→yellow, yellow→green, but I didn't have a distinct symbol for red! Let me fix that this turn with a clearer, corrected code, and specifically confirm blue→red mapping since that's the one that matters now.

I'll define: 👍=blue, ✌=green, 🖐=yellow, 👌=red (new symbol for red). Then send the specific relevant mapping: blue(👍) → red(👌), to make sure Deaf knows to tell Blind "cut red" (wire 3).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot understand gestures without a shared meaning yet. Display still 0, light still blue, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. If you want me to confirm something, use thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, and I will answer only through Blind since I cannot speak to you after this turn ends the round.

Deaf has proposed a simple yes/no protocol using 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. This is great - I can use this to confirm/deny hypotheses. Deaf says light is blue, wires are 1=green, 2=yellow, 3=red.

According to my manual: blue → cut red. Wire 3 is red. So the answer is: cut wire 3.

I need to communicate "wire 3" to Deaf using only yes/no confirmable gestures. Since Deaf now understands 👍=yes, 👎=no, I can ask a yes/no question... but wait, I can't ask questions with words, I can only gesture. I need to encode "wire 3" somehow using gestures Deaf can interpret, or use the yes/no scheme in reverse - I make a guess, Deaf confirms via Blind (but Deaf can't gesture back easily since gestures are one-way from me).

Actually, I should propose an encoding: I'll gesture a number of taps to indicate wire number. Let me send 3 identical gesture symbols to mean "wire 3", and 👍 to mean "confirmed by manual" as this is correct.

Let me try: send ☝✌🤟 style counting isn't standard, but I can use repetition of a symbol as a count. I'll send 👉👉👉 (three times) to indicate "3", paired with 👍 to indicate "this is the one, correct/cut this one".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "👉", "👉", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👉 👉 👉 👍]

Deaf just echoed back my exact gesture: [👉👉👉👍]. This seems to be a repeat/mirror, possibly Deaf is confirming they received it correctly by mirroring it back to me, or perhaps Deaf mixed up sending vs receiving and just gestured what they saw. Either way, this confirms my message reached Deaf clearly (three 👉 then 👍).

Now I need to know if Deaf understood the meaning: "wire 3, cut it". Since Deaf said they'll answer only through Blind now (once this round ends), Deaf may not gesture back with new info again after this. I should reinforce the meaning clearly one more time in case my intent wasn't understood, and also introduce a distinct "cut" signal separate from confirmation.

Let me clarify: I'll gesture "cut" concept association - repeat the pattern but add a distinct marker for "action=cut" versus counting. I'll use 👉 x3 for "three", and ✌ (already used for green in my earlier failed code) - let me pick a fresh unambiguous symbol for "cut": use ✊ for "cut this wire".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "👉", "👉", "✊"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports wire 3 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 1 is green. Display reads 0, light is blue. Waiting for instructions on which wire to cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👉 👉 👉 ✊]

Excellent - now I have direct confirmation. Blind heard from Deaf (via speech) the full wire layout: 1=green, 2=yellow, 3=red, light=blue. Blind is now waiting for instructions on which wire to cut. Deaf also mirrored my gesture back exactly [👉👉👉✊], confirming they received "three, cut" clearly.

Now, critically - Blind is asking ME for instructions, but I cannot speak to Blind at all! I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. I have no direct channel to Blind.

So the real solution: I need Deaf to be the one who tells Blind which wire to cut, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear. Deaf already knows the wire colors (from their own sight) and now has received my gesture "three, cut" which should mean "cut wire 3". Deaf needs to relay this verbally to Blind.

I should reinforce this one more time to be fully sure, and perhaps encode it more redundantly since lives are at stake - blue light maps to red wire, which is wire 3. My gesture already conveys "wire 3, cut". Deaf should now speak to Blind: "cut wire 3."

Since I can't speak to Blind directly, my job is done once Deaf has the info. Let me send one final confirming gesture to Deaf to make sure they act on it now, and also acknowledge I understand Blind is waiting.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "👉", "👉", "✊", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf gestured back a simple 👍 - acknowledging/confirming they understood my message "three, cut, confirmed" (wire 3, cut it, yes). This strongly suggests Deaf now understands they should tell Blind to cut wire 3.

At this point, my role is essentially complete - I've successfully communicated "cut wire 3" to Deaf through the gesture channel. Deaf can now speak this instruction to Blind, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear speech. I have no direct channel to Blind, so there's nothing more for me to add unless something changes.

I'll wait and see if further clarification is needed, but I don't want to send redundant noise that could confuse the established protocol. Let me send one more clear confirmation to be safe, in case Deaf is asking "is this correct?" with their thumbs up as a question back to me rather than an acknowledgment.

Actually, re-reading: Deaf earlier said "use thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, and I will answer only through Blind." This 👍 might be Deaf's own confirmation signal meaning "yes, I understood, I will act." I'll respond with a final 👍 to close the loop affirmatively.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
